question:
A 25-year-old woman presents to the clinic with complaints of dysuria and increased urinary frequency. Her urinalysis results are negative for nitrites. Urine microscopy shows the findings in figure A.

What is the most likely cause underlying her symptoms?
analysis: The presence of white blood cells (WBCs) and red blood cells (RBCs) in the urine microscopy suggests a urinary tract infection (UTI). The absence of nitrites makes E. coli infection less likely, as nitrites are typically produced by E. coli. S. saprophyticus is a common cause of UTI in young women and is more likely in this case.
